messages.content: What is the time difference between Los Angeles and Berlin?

function.name: get_co_ordinate
function.description: Fetch geographical coordinates of a particular location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city name you want coordinates for.

message.content:
Los Angeles (PST/PDT) is normally **UTC‑08:00** during Standard Time and **UTC‑07:00** when Daylight Saving Time (DST) is observed.  
Berlin (CET/CEST) is usually **UTC+01:00** under Standard Time and shifts forward one hour to **UTC+02:00** during DST.

Because both regions observe DST at roughly the same times of year (the U.S. starts DST second Sunday in March and ends first Sunday in November; Europe begins DST last Sunday in March and ends last Sunday in October), their relative offset stays constant throughout most of the year:

| Period | Los Angeles Offset | Berlin Offset | Difference |
|--------|--------------------|---------------|------------|
| Winter (roughly Nov–Mar) | UTC‑08:00 | UTC+01:00 | **+9 hours** ahead |
| Summer (roughly Mar–Oct) | UTC‑07:00 | UTC+02:00 | **+9 hours** ahead |

So regardless of whether each side is on Standard or Daylight Time, Berlin is typically nine hours *ahead* of Los Angeles.  

If you’re looking for an exact local‑time conversion right now, just add 9 hours to whatever time it’s currently in Los Angeles. For example, if it’s 2 PM PDT there, it will be 11 PM CEST in Berlin.

But can approximate based on standard offsets: PST UTC−8 vs CET UTC+1 gives +9 hours difference. However daylight savings may change it. Without dynamic info, maybe mention typical ranges.
